root_cause.text: The Bluetooth virtio_bt driver’s virtbt_rx_handle() strips the leading pkt_type byte and passes the skb to hci_recv_frame() without validating that the remaining skb->len is at least the fixed HCI header size for the selected packet type, allowing the HCI core to read past available initialized packet data.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “none of the switch cases in virtbt_rx_handle() check skb->len against the per-type minimum HCI header size before handing the frame to the core,” and the patch adds per-type min_hdr checks (event 2, ACL 4, SCO 3, ISO 4) before calling hci_recv_frame(), fixing cases where a one-byte completion left skb->len at 0 and led to dereferencing hci_acl_hdr(skb)->handle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local `min_hdr` variable in `virtbt_rx_handle()` to support forthcoming minimum-header-length handling in packet receive processing.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `size_t min_hdr;`, was added at the beginning of `virtbt_rx_handle()` before the existing `pkt_type` declaration.
intent_record.how: At runtime this specific hunk alone does not change behavior, but it prepares the function to track a minimum header length value, likely for upcoming packet-size validation or parsing logic within the receive path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate received virtio Bluetooth packet lengths against their HCI header sizes before dispatching them, dropping malformed packets safely and logging the error.
intent_record.what: The switch in virtbt_rx_handle() was changed so each recognized HCI packet type assigns a corresponding minimum header size to min_hdr and breaks, instead of immediately passing HCI_ISODATA_PKT to hci_recv_frame(); the default case now frees the skb and returns; after the switch, a new length check rejects packets whose skb->len is smaller than min_hdr with a ratelimited error log, frees the skb, and returns; only after this validation does the code set hci_skb_pkt_type(skb) and call hci_recv_frame(vbt->hdev, skb).
intent_record.how: At runtime, all supported received Bluetooth packet types are now validated to ensure they contain at least their required HCI header before being handed to the HCI core. This prevents undersized or malformed packets from being processed, avoids passing invalid buffers downstream, and adds diagnostic logging when such packets are dropped. It also makes ISO packets follow the same validation-and-dispatch path as the other packet types.

grouping_result.intent: Add a local `min_hdr` variable in `virtbt_rx_handle()` to support forthcoming minimum-header-length handling in packet receive processing.
Validate received virtio Bluetooth packet lengths against their HCI header sizes before dispatching them, dropping malformed packets safely and logging the error.

relevance_review.reason: The change introduces a minimum-header-length variable directly in virtbt_rx_handle(), which is the function implicated in failing to validate that skb->len meets the required HCI header size after stripping pkt_type. This is preparatory work for the missing length check tied to the root cause.

The change directly addresses the root cause by adding packet-length validation after stripping the pkt_type and before passing frames to HCI processing, ensuring the remaining skb length is sufficient for the expected HCI header and dropping malformed packets safely.

candidates.rationale: This dispatches the packet to the HCI core after only stripping/setting packet type, without first ensuring skb->len is large enough for the fixed HCI header of the selected packet type, enabling out-of-bounds reads of uninitialized packet data.
This marks the skb as a specific HCI packet type and is part of the path that forwards malformed short packets without validating the remaining length against that type's minimum header size.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the sink that forwards the received skb into the HCI core after the leading pkt_type byte was stripped, but before any check that the remaining skb->len is at least the fixed HCI header size required for that packet type. As a result, malformed short packets can cause the HCI core to read past available initialized packet data.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `virtbt_rx_handle()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The function reads the packet type from `skb->data` (`pkt_type = *((__u8 *) skb->data);`), then unconditionally removes that byte with `skb_pull(skb, 1);`, and for recognized packet types immediately forwards the skb via `hci_recv_frame(vbt->hdev, skb);`. There is no validation that the remaining `skb->len` after stripping the type byte is at least the required fixed HCI header size for `HCI_EVENT_PKT`, `HCI_ACLDATA_PKT`, `HCI_SCODATA_PKT`, or `HCI_ISODATA_PKT`. This exactly matches the described root cause: the driver strips the leading `pkt_type` and passes the skb to the HCI core without checking that enough bytes remain for the selected packet type's header. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.
